question.text: A metallic rod of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is placed in North-South direction and is moved at a constant speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> towards East. The horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field at that place is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> and the angle of dip is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. The emf induced in the rod is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mV</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Emf produced is ε=BVL⊥v⊥

We know BVBH=tan45°, so BV=4×10-3 T

Then,  ε=4×10-3×20×10-2×20 =16 mV
